about.title: Eureka Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Humboldt County saw 4 traffic deaths alongside 214 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, numbers that translate into real families across Eureka now facing sudden, unexpected loss. Corridors like Broadway Street, Rt 101, H Street, and I Street carry heavy local traffic, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see the most reported crashes. When a collision takes a spouse, parent, or child, surviving family members are left not only grieving but also managing funeral costs, lost income, and an uncertain path forward. California law allows certain family members to pursue a wrongful death claim to recover some of those losses, but the process involves strict deadlines and specific rules about who may file. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply listen to what happened, then connect your family with an independent attorney in our network who can explain your options in plain terms, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Eureka Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing mainly to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents and heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands before any claim moves forward.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Deadline
items.desc: California generally requires a wrongful death claim to be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window can be shorter when a government entity is involved. Missing this deadline can close the door on recovery, so timing matters.

items.title: Losses the Law Recognizes
items.desc: California allows families to seek compensation for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. These losses are separate from any criminal case that may also follow the same crash.

items.question: How is a wrongful death claim different from a criminal case?
items.answer: A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment for the driver or party at fault. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action brought by the family to recover financial losses like funeral costs and lost support. One case can move forward regardless of the outcome of the other.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to explain who qualifies.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a busy Eureka road like Broadway or H Street?
items.answer: The road itself doesn't change your legal rights, but knowing where and when a crash occurred, including patterns like Friday evening traffic on corridors such as Broadway Street or Rt 101, can help an attorney understand the full picture. Local crash data can sometimes support the investigation into how the collision happened.

items.question: What does it cost to talk with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your family recovers compensation.
